articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Liverpool host Arsenal in blockbuster clash
articles.description: Liverpool welcome Arsenal to Anfield in a huge clash, with both sides looking to make a statement in the Premier League title race.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ速報：リヴァプールとアーセナルが注目のビッグマッチで激突
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグのタイトル争いで存在感を示そうとする両チームが、アンフィールドで対戦する。
articles.body:
It's the first day of November, and we've got a massive Premier League showdown on our hands as Liverpool welcome Arsenal to Anfield in a clash between two of England's biggest clubs.

The defending champions have won seven of their opening eight league matches, and Mikel Arteta's side will be looking to maintain their strong start to the season. However, they face a Liverpool side finding its rhythm under Andoni Iraola, with the Reds hoping to close the six-point gap between the teams.

There's also plenty of history at stake, with Arsenal looking to secure their first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012.

Follow along for all the latest updates, goals, highlights and analysis from our experts.

articles.headline: The Patriots are 18-43 all time in Miami. Here are keys to a Week 8 victory
articles.description: Former Patriots player and current TV analyst Logan Ryan details what he thinks New England needs to improve on vs. Miami.
articles.headlineJa: ペイトリオッツのマイアミ戦通算成績は18勝43敗。第8週勝利への鍵とは
articles.descriptionJa: 元ペイトリオッツの選手で現在はテレビ解説を務めるローガン・ライアンが、ニューイングランドがマイアミ戦で改善すべき点について詳述する。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

1. Uncharacteristic Pats: When former Patriots cornerback and two-time Super Bowl champion Logan Ryan was preparing for the television broadcast of Sunday's game between New England and Miami (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS), one of the things that excited him most was to share his analysis of receiver A.J. Brown.

He was ready to declare it "the A.J. Brown game," adding how he knows Brown's "mindset and mentality" from their time as teammates with the Tennessee Titans.

But as often happens in the NFL, Ryan had to be prepared to pivot, a result of Brown having his knee flare up and not being able to finish Wednesday's practice before missing the rest of the week. 

Brown was officially ruled out Saturday, along with running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness), which continues a season-long theme of managing the roster due to a relentless run of injuries.

The game still remains very much in Ryan's wheelhouse because of his connections to both teams -- having played for Patriots coach Mike Vrabel in Tennessee, as well as alongside veteran New England safety Kevin Byard, and crediting Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley for hatching his NFL playing career after playing for him when Hafley was defensive backs coach at Rutgers.

What stands out to Ryan about the Patriots from his film study?

"I see a well-coached and balanced team with too many uncharacteristic turnovers [14, second most in the NFL]. I know that is not a Mike Vrabel team with the turnovers. And I see too many missed tackles defensively holding them back in terms of the next step in consistency," he said of a defense that has forced just seven turnovers.

"Sometimes when chasing turnovers defensively, you miss tackles because you're not securing it first. I'm sure [Vrabel] continues to preach the fundamentals but it's an uncharacteristic kind of spell they've been in."

New England's 34 missed tackles are 14th most in the NFL, just above the league average of 33.4 missed tackles per team, according to ESPN Research. They had a season-high 11 missed tackles against the Bears last week, but Ryan believes better results should come.

He noted the 10-day stretch since that game, which provided more time to tighten things up, and he's curious to see how that manifests itself against a 1-5 team coming off its first victory of the season -- 28-25 over the Jets on the road.

He also will be watching how much Drake Maye is on the run -- by choice or not -- and if the Patriots can bottle up quarterback Malik Willis as a rushing threat (223 yards on the ground, second most among QBs).

"These are two of the top scrambling quarterbacks in the NFL and I'm not sure people understand how good Drake Maye (211 yards, fifth among QBs) is running and extending plays with his legs," he said.

articles.headline: Miami Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas rounding into form ahead of Pats matchup
articles.description: The rookie wide receiver has impressed Dolphins coaches with his production on and off the ball.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ドルフィンズのWRカレブ・ダグラス、ペイトリオッツ戦を前に調子を上げてくる
articles.descriptionJa: この新人ワイドレシーバーは、プレー中およびプレー外での活躍でドルフィンズのコーチ陣に好印象を与えている。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- It's been a while since Caleb Douglas was on the sideline.

The Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver, who played all 27 possible games at Texas Tech over his final two collegiate seasons, would have to go back to his two years at Florida to find an extended period of time when he did not play.

So when he missed three games this season with an ankle injury, it was new territory for him.

"It's not easy," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said last week. "For some people, it might be easy. For some people, it's a challenge. There are some guys that can learn by watching; there are some people that actually have to learn by doing. So I think it's different with every player.

"Ultimately, the more you can actually do it, the timing, the rhythm, getting comfortable back with the quarterback, but mentally, he has stayed sharp because he's been pretty efficient in practice. But again, you're talking about a rookie who hasn't played much football."

Douglas returned in the Dolphins' win over the New York Jets in Week 7, finishing with 70 yards and two touchdowns on two catches. His highlight play came on a 63-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the fourth quarter that effectively put the game out of reach.

But the third-round draft pick caught Hafley's attention with his work outside of his two scores, mainly the cleanliness of his procedural work despite the extended absence, and his effort in the run game.

"Those are the things that you worry about, right?" Hafley said. "We didn't have any of those errors from him. And those are, a lot of times the rookies, as you saw early in the year, that's not exactly easy for them ... And then his physicality in the run game. I thought he took a big step from where he was to when I turned on that tape and the way he was fighting with DBs. I thought that was pretty cool to see.

"And then obviously you had the one really good route in the red zone and then the catch and run down the sideline. Hopefully we'll get a chance to get him the ball more."

The Dolphins ran for 156 yards last week, their fifth straight game with more than 100 rushing yards. On a team that's dedicated to running the ball, it's critical that the receivers are willing to block.

"Blocking is 90% effort, 10% technique -- you got to want to do it," Dolphins receivers coach Tyke Tolbert said. "I just believe that it's all about want-to ... it's really about the effort and showing up for your teammates in the run game or letting somebody else catch the ball, turn and block the man covering you.

"That's the easiest thing to do. We'll call it a flip and find. Got to flip and find somebody to block. It's a want-to and it's more effort than anything."

Dolphins receiver Malik Washington executed the "flip and find" on Douglas' second touchdown catch, acting as a lead blocker as Douglas ran down the sideline -- which the rookie thanked the veteran for after the game.

articles.headline: Will usually active Jets play or pass before trade deadline?
articles.description: New York could look to add to its pile of assets ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.headlineJa: 動きのあるジェッツは、トレード期限前に動くのか、それとも静観するのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ニューヨークは11月10日のトレード期限を前に、戦力を強化する動きを見せる可能性がある。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets:

1. Ready, set, trade: General manager Darren Mougey has executed 14 player trades in 14 months, so it's easy to assume he will be wheeling and dealing as the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches. Don't be surprised if that's not the case.

There won't be a sell-off like last year (see: Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams blockbusters). There might not be anything splashy. It feels like the Jets (2-5) are leaning toward standing pat. Of course, never say "never" with Mougey.

Let's examine where the Jets stand regarding trade candidates.

Wide receiver Garrett Wilson generated the most buzz this week after frustration spilled into the media -- with him having to answer questions about if he wanted to be traded or not and ESPN's Adam Schefter reporting Saturday that there's "no way" that the Jets would deal their star wideout. Wilson told reporters that he won't ask for a trade despite his lack of targets in recent weeks amid the losing. Stay tuned, though. This could be an offseason storyline, especially if things don't improve.

Braelon Allen's emergence at running back has fueled speculation about Breece Hall, but would the Jets trade him six months after giving him a three-year, $43.5 million extension? It happened to Gardner last year. In this case, it seems unlikely.

The Jets believe that they have the NFL's best 1-2 punch, and they don't want to break it up. Even if they wanted to move him, Hall's recent injuries may give teams pause. He has missed four games because of a quadriceps injury after missing a chunk of training camp because of a strained groin.

More realistic trade candidates:

Will McDonald IV: Remember when coach Aaron Glenn boasted about how they would coach him up, turning him into an all-around force? That was a year ago. The former first-round pick is now a part-time player with only two sacks and four quarterback hits. But he has pass-rushing ability (10.5 sacks in 2024), so there will be interest. Former Jets coach Jeff Ulbrich is the Atlanta Falcons' defensive coordinator, and he could use an edge rusher. McDonald, due a guaranteed $13.8 million in 2027, could bring back a fourth- or fifth-round pick.

Nahshon Wright: He told ESPN that he's frustrated and open to a trade, a sentiment he said he shared with the organization. It seemed to be a good signing at the time, a noted ballhawk (five interceptions last season with the Chicago Bears) joining a team that had no picks in 2025. It hasn't worked out, as he has yet to play a defensive snap. He's on a one-year deal for $3.5 million.

Jarvis Brownlee Jr.: He was a healthy scratch last week because he missed multiple mandatory meetings, leading to a team fine, Brownlee told ESPN. He might be back in the lineup this week, but rookie D'Angelo Ponds is waiting in the wings at nickel back. Acquired in a September 2025 trade, Brownlee is on a team-friendly contract through 2027.

articles.headline: Ranking the top 10 trick plays in Super Bowl history
articles.description: Which trick plays cemented their legacies in the Super Bowl? We listed 10 that changed momentum or flat-out won championships.
articles.headlineJa: スーパーボウル史上、最高のトリックプレー・トップ10
articles.descriptionJa: スーパーボウルでその名を歴史に刻んだトリックプレーとは？試合の流れを変えたり、そのまま優勝を決定づけたりした10のプレーをリストアップした。
articles.body:
The Super Bowl is the biggest stage in American sports. Millions of people tune in to see the final two teams remaining from the NFL playoffs.

It's the perfect time for a coach to dig into his bag of tricks and give his players a chance to do the unexpected. But it's also a high-risk, high-reward decision. If it goes right, the coach is a genius, but if it doesn't, his decision will be questioned forever.

Dialing up a trick play at just the right time can catch the opponent slipping and lead to a huge momentum shift, such as Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Nick Foles catching a touchdown pass that led to an upset victory over the New England Patriots. It could also put a game out of reach, such as quarterback Phil Simms' flea-flicker pass to Phil McConkey that put the New York Giants two scores ahead of the Denver Broncos.

Here are the 10 most memorable trick plays in Super Bowl history:

COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series, featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, that will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027.

1. Philly Special

When: Super Bowl LII -- Feb. 4, 2018

Team: Philadelphia Eagles

Opponent: New England Patriots

Situation: The Eagles were leading 15-12 in the second quarter and facing fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line.

Philadelphia desperately needed to answer the Patriots' touchdown, which trimmed New England's deficit to 15-12. Eagles coach Doug Pederson went for it rather than kick the field goal. Coming away with anything less than a touchdown going into halftime, leading by three points, would have been a deflating result for the Eagles, considering New England got the ball back to start the third quarter.

"When you're playing the Patriots and Tom Brady, field goals don't win games," Pederson said after the game.

Pederson called a timeout to talk things over with quarterback Nick Foles, who uttered the now-famous words, "Do you want Philly, Philly?" Foles was originally lined up in a shotgun formation before walking to the right side of the offensive line, next to tackle Lane Johnson.

Jason Kelce snapped the ball directly to running back Corey Clement, pitched the ball to tight end Trey Burton as Foles leaked to the back of the end zone. Burton lofted the pass to a wide-open Foles to put the Eagles up 22-12 at halftime. Philadelphia went on to win 41-33 to secure the first Super Bowl victory in team history.

2. "Ambush" onside kick

When: Super Bowl XLIV -- Feb. 7, 2010

Team: New Orleans Saints

Opponent: Indianapolis Colts

Situation:  The Saints were trailing 10-6 at halftime.

Manchester United are a mess. The storied club are in a relegation battle after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea extended the club's winless run to nine games. But which players have been linked with a move to Old Trafford in recent months? Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

Manchester United have been linked with a host of players who could improve their squad, so let's break them down by position:

Goalkeeper

Senne Lammens is safe in the No. 1 spot for now, but veteran backups Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton will need replacing, while André Onana is still on the books and is at Trabzonspor on loan.

- United could target Gianluigi Donnarumma from Manchester City if the club are thrown out of the league over their financial breaches. (Daily Express)

- Athletic Club and Spain star Unai Simón has been previously linked, but says he would turn down a €150 million offer to stay at Athletic. (Marca)

- The agent of Paraguay international goalkeeper Orlando Gill said in July: "There were enquiries with Manchester United." But he moved to Lille in August. (DSports Radio)

Defense

Lisandro Martínez hit out at United's hierarchy about the lack of signings, and defense is the key area they failed to strengthen in the summer. After recent issues, it's fair to say Martinez will need replacing too. Left back is the main area of interest here.

Full back

- Newcastle United's Lewis Hall was a key target before he signed a new long-term contract in September. (ESPN)

- AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert recently earned a recall to the France national team and has been linked. (iNews)

-  Alejandro Balde's future at Barcelona has been the subject of much discussion recently, with a reported loan deal in January on the cards. (TEAMtalk)

- Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell has caught the eye of United scouts, as well as those from Liverpool. (TEAMtalk)

Center back

- Fulham captain Calvin Bassey, 26, has been in good form this season and has appeared on United's radar. (TEAMtalk)

- United are reported to be among the frontrunners for 24-year-old Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, and have remained interested since they had an offer worth £45 million turned down for him in 2024. (Football Insider)

- FC Como star Jacobo Ramón caught the eye in their UCL win. (TEAMtalk)

- Nottingham Forest defender Murillo has been linked with a £70 million move. (TEAMtalk)

- RB Leipzig Castello Lukeba could be available for around €65 million and is reportedly a long-term target. (Fussball)

- Bayer Leverkusen's Edmond Tapsoba remains one of the key targets for Manchester United. (Ekrem Konur)

Midfield

United spent over £150 million to bring in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba this summer. But now they need an upgrade or two. And they may need to replace captain Bruno Fernandes next summer too.

articles.headline: Robert De Zerbi on Tottenham revival: 'Now we are playing as a team'
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham's turnaround in the Premier League is down to his new-look squad now being a team.
articles.headlineJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビが語るトッテナム復活：「今、私たちはチームとしてプレーできている」
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビは、プレミアリーグにおけるトッテナムの好転は、刷新されたスカッドが真の「チーム」になったことによるものだと考えている。
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham's turnaround in the Premier League is down to his new-look squad now being a team.

Spurs produced a professional display to beat 10-man Crystal Palace by a 2-0 score on Saturday to win three consecutive league games for the first time in 616 days.

A trip to Marbella last month has been the catalyst for this form and after £380 million ($509m) was committed on 10 new signings this summer by majority owners the Lewis family, De Zerbi believes Tottenham are finally a team again.

"I think even before the national break we were playing well," De Zerbi said.

"We were playing maybe not 90 minutes, but many parts of the game we played very well. We didn't score. We conceded a stupid goal and then we lost energy. We lost spirit. We lost the right union between the players.

"If we compare Tottenham before the national break and Tottenham after the national break, now we are playing as a team.

"Before the national break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team."

The growing camaraderie in this Spurs side has been evident and was again on Saturday with opening scorer Archie Gray mobbed by the home substitutes on the sideline after his 25th-minute headed goal.

Gray produced another accomplished display at right-back on the ninth occasion the 20-year-old has started out of position this season.

De Zerbi took off Gray at half-time, but it was down to a yellow card in the 15th minute.

"He's improving a lot. After Manchester United, he's playing very, very well and as a mature player," De Zerbi said.

"I didn't want to take a risk for another yellow card. I'm sorry because he was playing very well.

"I explained why I took the decision, but I think it was the right decision in that moment."

Gray's growing comfort at right-back has allowed De Zerbi and Tottenham to be patient with World Cup winner Pedro Porro, who missed the start of the campaign with a hamstring issue.

The same injury was aggravated in a September defeat to Aston Villa, but Porro is fit again and will be ready to start next week's trip to Leeds if required.

De Zerbi explained: "Pedro is ready. We didn't take risks. Speaking with him, he decided before the game [to not start] and he was very honest with me.

"And I appreciate a lot because the Premier League is 38 games, not one game."

- Under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage: 'I will never give up'

Porro and Destiny Udogie featured in tandem on opposite flanks during the second half in another sign of Spurs' improved squad depth.

Both have been crucial to De Zerbi's predecessors, but given Udogie has struggled with multiple fitness problems, the free signing of Andy Robertson in June has alleviated Spurs' reliance on the Italian.

Robertson has produced a string of consistent performances and De Zerbi has challenged Udogie to stay fit for a sustained period.

articles.headline: Arsenal's Bruno Guimarães on unique penalty technique: 'Not working anymore'
articles.description: Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimarães has admitted that his penalty technique "is not working anymore," saying that he has to change the way he takes them in an exclusive interview with ESPN Brasil.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルのブルーノ・ギマランイス、独特なPK技術について：「もう通用していない」
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルのミッドフィールダー、ブルーノ・ギマランイスは、ESPN Brasilとの独占インタビューの中で、自身のPK技術が「もう通用していない」と認め、蹴り方を変える必要があると語った。
articles.body:
Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimarães has admitted that his penalty technique "is not working anymore," saying that he has to change the way he takes them in an exclusive interview with ESPN Brasil. 

Guimarães' stutter-step penalty style has come under the spotlight in recent weeks with the Brazilian's missed penalty the reason for Arsenal's shootout defeat to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup last week. 

It joined an alarming recent record from the spot with Guimarães missing three out of his last four penalties for his club and country. 

"Look, I think I've been taking my penalties in a certain way. I tried it during the World Cup, and I tried it here, too. It's clear to me now that it's not working anymore," Guimarães told ESPN Brasil. 

"I'm humble enough to acknowledge that I need to improve and that I have to change the way I take them. But one thing is certain: this doesn't change who I am as a player or as a person.

"As I said, I'm humble enough to admit that my recent penalty kicks haven't been good. My record before the World Cup was very strong, but lately, I haven't been able to deliver at that same level. It's something I need to work on, I have to train differently.

"Life doesn't stop, and the challenges keep coming. We have another match this Sunday, and if I let this get to me, I'll only spiral downward.

"Or should I turn things around instead? I need to mature through my mistakes and learn from them. I've already decided that I shouldn't continue taking them the way I was."

Guimarães also said he takes "three or four" penalty kicks every training session as he aims to restore his positive spot-kick record. 

"I think the most important thing is not to be afraid of what might happen, it's about putting in the work during training so that when the moment arrives, I'm ready," he said.

- Arsenal's Dowman handed three-game ban for red card after appeal rejected 

"Every single day now, I take at least three or four penalty kicks, I want to be prepared in case it happens again. I can't let my teammates down, and I can't let our people down.

"We know it can happen [missing penalty kicks], we saw it at the World Cup, with Messi missing a penalty, Mbappé missing one, and plenty of others missing as well. It's obviously a situation we'd rather avoid, but I'm humble enough to recognize when something isn't going right.

"What I need to do is work even harder so that when the next opportunity comes along, I can step up and not let it go to waste."

articles.body:
ESPN's weekly running back fantasy football rankings are an aggregate of our eight rankers. Listed alphabetically, they are Matt Bowen, Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft, Daniel Dopp, Eric Karabell, Liz Loza, Eric Moody and Field Yates.

Rankings for the week will be published every Tuesday and weigh the player's skills and role in the offense, as well as the quality of that week's matchup, and are updated throughout the week for news and emerging analysis.

articles.headline: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick on Lamine Yamal: 'Easier' to substitute when he scores
articles.description: Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナのハンジ・フリック監督、ラミン・ヤマルについて：「彼がゴールを決めれば、交代させやすい」
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日にスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウで行われたラ・リーガのアラベス戦（6-1で勝利）で活躍したラミン・ヤマルについて、ハンジ・フリック監督は、彼がゴールを決めた後であれば交代させるのも容易だと語った。
articles.body:
Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.

Yamal netted a brace as Barça returned to winning ways after back-to-back defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

The teenager has now started all 18 games for Barça and Spain this season, although he was afforded a short rest against Alavés, with Flick able to take him off for the final 20 minutes with the game won.

"When you score two goals, it's easier to go out," Flick said after substituting Yamal for just the fourth time this season.

"I spoke with him at half time [about managing his minutes]. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half [is good], but it also important he has less minutes."

Barça opened the scoring early on through Raphinha before Fermín López added the second in the 23rd minute.

Raphinha's second of the game, and his 17th of the season, made it 3-0 and Yamal capped a fine team move with a brilliant finish from the edge of the box to make it four by half time.

Yamal netted another after the break, a dinked finish over the goalkeeper initially ruled out for offside, and Anthony Gordon scored the sixth late on prior to an even later consolation goal from Mariano Díaz.

It was just what Barça needed after a week which saw their 11-game winning run halted by losses to PSG in the Champions League and Madrid in the league.

"For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermín, Rapha," Flick added.

"This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way."

Flick also had praise for his makeshift defence, with midfielder Frenkie de Jong featuring at centre-back and youngster Brian Fariñas, also a midfielder, making his full debut at right-back.

"At the moment we have to think different," Flick said. "Four defenders are out in Xavi Espart, Andreas [Christensen], Jules [Koundé] and Eric Garcìa.

"Hopefully some will come back, but we don't know when yet. So I asked Frenkie if he's able to play there; he said 'Yes, when I can help the team I will do it.'

"The same with Brian. I don't know if he ever played [at right-back], maybe in La Masia, but he also played a good level.

"I am happy for him. He deserved these minutes, this game. He is focused, top in training, very professional. This is what we want from him and the players."

- Gordon, Yamal, Raphinha on target as Barcelona hit Alavés for six

Fariñas, 20, looked especially comfortable playing on the same flank as Yamal, someone he played with at youth level.

"You could see he is connected with Lamine," Flick continued. "It's very important. He helped us a lot today playing this position."

The win took Barça back to the top of the table after Atlético Madrid had leapfrogged them earlier on Saturday.
